submission.bindingBasis: The planning evidence binds to revision 3 and checkpoint frontier=beta-concurrent. The consequence boundary evidence states ownerChanged: true with the Task revision advancing after planning, so the expected revision is stale and the checkpoint action would fail with REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed under the contract.
submission.rationale: The owner contract states: "task.checkpoint requires expectedRevision" and "stale expectedRevision fails REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed". The boundary evidence confirms the revision advanced after planning (ownerChanged: true). Semantically, the intended consequence requires checking whether the newer Task state still supports the beta-complete transition. We cannot rely on planning-time evidence since the owner has changed. We should re-observe the current Task state (revision, frontier) before deciding whether the checkpoint is still applicable, would need a rebase, or is no longer valid. Acting now with the stale revision would predictably fail; holding forever preserves no progress; and rebasing/acting cannot be correctly decided without fresh observation of the owner's actual current state.
